title: C struct padding
author: Drishtant Ghosh

scenes.headline: Double the L1 cache misses.
scenes.sub: The culprit was member ordering, not the algorithm.

scenes.caption: Logically 6 bytes. sizeof says 12.

scenes.label: 3 padding bytes after a, then the struct rounds up to a multiple of 4.

scenes.title: Fix it in review
items: Profile L1 misses, not just big-O

slides.title: Compilers align members
slides.body: Members are aligned to their size or the CPU word size. To make that work, the compiler inserts padding bytes you never declared.

slides.title: 6 bytes on paper
slides.caption: int b cannot start at address 1, so it starts at 4. sizeof is 12, not 6.

slides.label: for a payload that is 16 bytes on paper
slides.body: Careless member ordering doubled the footprint and doubled L1 cache misses.

slides.title: Order members largest to smallest.
slides.body: Follow for daily systems engineering & code teardowns.

caption: A 16-byte struct that is really 32 bytes. Struct padding, explained before your coffee cools. Which struct in your codebase would you check first?
